name: c-make
title: GNU Make
summary: The same integration with no helpers at all -- just the dsdlc command line and GNU Make. Worth reading even if you use CMake, because it shows what `dsdlc_generate()` is doing on your behalf: a query for the file lists, a stamp to stand in for a multiple-output rule, and depfiles for the dependencies nothing else can work out.
notes: Portable back to GNU Make 3.81, which is what macOS still ships -- hence the stamp file rather than 4.3's grouped targets (`&:`). Two independent sets of depfiles are included: dsdlc's `-MD`, which records the definitions behind each generated file, and the C compiler's `-MMD`, which records the headers behind each object. They answer different questions and neither substitutes for the other.

requires.reason: compiles the generated C and the round-trip program
